`App.tsx`: un solo estado de carga y un despacho exhaustivo
summary: App.tsx now holds one SummaryLoad per load, asks ScreenChoice.of for the dashboard and dispatches the body with a module-level screenBody(screen, shell): ReactElement whose switch has no default branch (proved: dropping one case makes tsc fail with TS2366); setError and repoNameOf are gone and a folder without .git draws its designed screen with the clone list. Five things a reviewer should know. (1) The first Verification command, test "$(grep -c 'Cargando…' web/src/App.tsx web/src/App.test.tsx)" -eq 0, cannot pass as written: grep -c over two files prints one 'file:count' line per file, so test gets a two-line non-integer and exits 2 whatever the code says. Both counts are in fact 0 - 'Cargando…' is gone from both files - and the other three commands are green (npm test -w web 0, npm run build 0, npm run lint 0). (2) The brief's Call site passes history and snapshot to Header, but HeaderProps still requires meta and Header.tsx is task 6's file (its Files line carries Header.tsx and App.tsx), so passing them now breaks tsc; App keeps meta={load.status === 'loaded' ? load.summary.meta : null} and destructures only screen, leaving history and snapshot for task 6 to wire. (3) screenBody(screen: Screen) as the brief signs it cannot draw two of its five members - not-a-git-repo needs onRepo and blocks needs repoId and window - so the module-level function takes a second typed parameter Shell { repoId, window, onRepo }; everything else about it is as the brief prescribes. (4) The brief's swap of the 'Cargando…' wait for 'Analizando alpha-clone…' would have left a vacuous wait: hand-checked, by the time the clone path is on screen the summary has already landed, so queryByText of the analysing headline is null on the first poll and the wait guarantees nothing. The load-finished proof in both tests is now the positive findByText('Pulso'), with the analysing headline asserted absent beside it. (5) 'changing the window asks the API for that window' was strengthened for the same reason: its old expect(urls.at(-1)).toContain('window=all') stayed green when the summary effect stopped depending on window, because the heat request carries the window too; it now pins the summary requests alone as ['12m', 'all']. Every new and modified assertion was seen to fail by breaking the one thing its name promises.

summary: App.tsx now holds a single `load: SummaryLoad` per load, asks ScreenChoice.of for the screen and dispatches it in a module-level `screenBody` switch with no default branch and a declared `ReactElement` return, so a sixth member of `Screen` breaks the build; `setError`, `repoNameOf` and the `Cargando…` paragraph are gone, and the folder without `.git` now reaches Screens.NotAGitRepo with its clone list instead of the generic failure line. Three deviations from the brief's blocks, all deliberate: (1) `<Header>` keeps its `meta` prop instead of receiving `history`/`snapshot`, because HeaderProps still requires `meta` and does not declare the other two — Header.tsx is task 6's file, so wiring them now would not compile; the consequence is that until task 6 lands the header still reads a nullable `meta` derived from `load`, i.e. the optional-for-absent-member that ScreenChoice.of's `history`/`snapshot` exist to remove, and those two members of the Dashboard are computed and dropped on the floor for one commit. (2) `screenBody(screen: Screen, shell: Shell)` takes a second typed parameter rather than the brief's single-argument signature, because `blocks` needs `repoId` and `window` for TrendPanel and HeatBlock and `not-a-git-repo` needs the `onRepo` callback, none of which the `Screen` vocabulary carries and none of which this task may add to screen.ts. (3) The brief's swap of the `Cargando…` wait for the analysing headline is kept as `expect(queryByText('Analizando alpha-clone…')).toBeNull()` but preceded by a positive `await findByText('Pulso')` in both modified tests: a bare wait for an absent string goes green on the first tick before anything has rendered, so on its own it would no longer prove the load finished. `changing the window asks the API for that window` also tightened its assertion to the summary requests only (`['12m', 'all']`), since the heat block carries the window in its URL too and must not be what makes it pass. Attempt 1 of this task produced this code and failed only on a malformed control command (`grep -c` over two files feeding `test`), corrected in the plan by a human before this attempt; this attempt verified the tree against the brief and changed nothing. Verification: all four commands exit 0 (old copy gone, no `repoNameOf`, 83 tests in 8 files passing, build and lint clean).

`Header.tsx` y `StaleNotice.tsx`: la frescura de la foto
summary: Header.tsx no longer takes `meta`: it takes `history: HeaderHistory` and `snapshot: SnapshotNotice` and dispatches each of the two lines under the repo name over its vocabulary with no default branch, so `last-commit` keeps today's text, `none` draws NO_HISTORY_META, `unknown` draws nothing, `fresh`/`stale` call their format.ts function and `never-fetched` draws nothing. The new module StaleNotice.tsx exposes `StaleNotice.Banner` as a static method of a class, and App.tsx destructures all three members of the Dashboard, hands `history`/`snapshot` to Header — closing the debt task 5 recorded — and draws the banner between header and body when `snapshot.kind === 'stale'`, with no `Traer cambios` button. Contrasted point by point against the real brief once it arrived (its Task 6 section is byte-identical to the frozen plan's, and its five ct convention documents and plan-yardstick sections are the same paste as task 5's): Objective, Files, both Contract blocks, the Current state citation, the constraining prose, TDD, the four literal test names and the four Verification commands all match the tree, and nothing was changed as a result. Four things a reviewer should know. (1) The two dispatch functions in Header declare `ReactElement | null`, not the bare `ReactElement` of the closed decision's wording, because the same brief requires `unknown` and `never-fetched` to draw nothing; the effect that decision asks for still holds — adding a member to `SnapshotNotice` in screen.ts fails the build in Header.tsx with TS2366 (checked, then reverted). App's `screenBody` keeps the bare `ReactElement` because every member of `Screen` draws something. (2) The existing test `without dates the header shows neither` had its arrange re-pointed: it used to make the header show nothing by nulling `summary.meta`, and freshness now comes from the `Clone`, so it passes `CloneMother.neverFetched()` instead. No test name was added or removed beyond the four the plan declares (18 in the file). The three new snapshot tests deliberately make `summary.meta` disagree with the clone, so a header that went back to reading `meta` fails them. (3) `SummaryMeta.fetchedAt` and `SummaryMeta.stale` are now read by nothing in the interface — two payload fields that have to agree with `Clone.fetchedAt`/`Clone.stale` and no longer have a consumer. I did not touch them: `web/src/api/types.ts` and the server are outside this task's Files line and the brief puts the payload out of scope. (4) The banner's geometry is the mockup's `isStale` block (flex, gap 16px, padding 12px 16px, 3px left border) but its two colours are derived from the existing accent-2 tokens — `color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-accent-2) 8%, var(--color-bg))` background and `var(--color-accent-2-700)` text — instead of the mockup's literal #fff1f4 and #790e3d, because `web/src/tokens.css` is not in the Files line so no token could be added and no .tsx in this repo carries a raw hex. App's `snapshot.kind === 'stale'` is the brief's literal expression and is a single-member guard rather than a second exhaustive switch on purpose: the exhaustive dispatch over `SnapshotNotice` lives once, in Header, and declaring the same partition twice is the antipattern conventions/decisions.md names. Verification re-run against the real brief: all four commands exit 0 (18 tests in App.test.tsx, no seven-day threshold anywhere under web/src, 87 tests in 8 files passing, build and lint clean).

`Pulse.tsx`: la ventana sin actividad y su llamada a la acción
summary: Pulse.tsx now dispatches over `activity` with no default branch: `series` keeps the svg and the window edges, `empty-window` replaces both with a 250px-tall box (same height, so the blocks grid does not jump) carrying `emptyWindowHeadline`, `emptyWindowSentence` and a second exhaustive dispatch over `cta` — `switch` paints a button labelled `emptyWindowCtaLabel(cta.window)` that calls `onWindow(cta.window)`, `already-there` paints none. App.tsx hands it `screen.activity`, `setWindow` and the `now` it already holds, through two new members of its `Shell` interface. Two things a reviewer should know. First, PulseProps carries a fourth prop, `now: Date`, that the brief's Contract block does not list: the same brief's prose requires it ('App.tsx le pasa `activity`, `onWindow` y el `now` que ya tiene') and `emptyWindowSentence` takes a Date, so the alternative was Pulse reading the clock itself, which would break the one-instant-per-render rule App.tsx documents; I followed the prose and am flagging the divergence from the block. Second, the `summaryWith` mother in App.test.tsx defaulted to `kpis.commits: 0`, which this task turns into the trigger of the empty window, so four existing tests would have silently stopped testing the chart (and 'the header shows the last commit and the fetch date' would have broken outright, because the empty-window sentence also says 'último commit'); its default is now `{ commits: 25, activeAuthors: 3, filesTouched: 12 }` and a named `NO_COMMITS_KPIS` constant is what the two empty-window tests opt into. Each of the three new assertions was broken by hand and seen to fail for the reason its name gives: no-op onClick gives ['12m','30d'] instead of ['12m','30d','12m'], a cta on `already-there` fails the absence, and an empty box on `series` loses `pulse-current`.
